items.headline: Anthropic publishes Claude containment architecture
items.diff_narrative: Saturday's top-of-mix Anthropic storyline was geographic footprint plus vulnerability disclosure — KiYoung Choi's appointment as Representative Director of Korea, the Milan office opening as Anthropic's sixth European footprint, and a Project Glasswing update crediting Claude Mythos Preview with 10,000+ high or critical findings across roughly 50 partners. Sunday opens a structurally distinct Anthropic storyline focused on the engineering posture for agent isolation rather than offices or AI-found vulnerabilities. Anthropic's engineering team published a detailed post titled "How we contain Claude across products" walking through the per-product sandbox stack: a gVisor container with seccomp syscall filtering on isolated infrastructure for Claude.ai with ephemeral per-session filesystems, OS-native process sandboxes for Claude Code (Seatbelt on macOS, Bubblewrap on Linux, with an 84% reduction in permission prompts after delegating command approvals to a model-based classifier), and full guest VMs for Claude Cowork on Apple's Virtualization framework on macOS and HCS on Windows with credentials held on the host and files mounted under read-only, read-write, or read-write-no-delete modes. Simon Willison amplified the post late Saturday and demonstrated the new posture by getting Claude Opus 4.8 in Claude Code for web to refactor Datasette Lite from Web Workers to service workers, shipping a working FastCGI demo and a Datasette 1.0a31 demo built fully under the sandboxed agent.

items.headline: Snowflake heads into Summit 26 with $6B AWS Graviton commit and Natoma acquisition
items.diff_narrative: Saturday's vendor-tape storyline was the SpaceX S-1 vs Musk $37.5 billion disclosure gap on the Anthropic Memphis Colossus 1 compute arrangement, set against the SPCX June 8 roadshow open at a $1.75T-$2T target range and ~$75B raise — an IPO-prospectus disclosure-language axis. Sunday opens a structurally different vendor storyline on the data-platform earnings-and-strategy axis ahead of the Summit-26 keynote. Snowflake stacked three pre-Summit catalysts inside the May 27-29 window: a $6 billion five-year commitment to AWS expanding Snowflake's use of Amazon's Graviton general-purpose chips and cloud GPUs for agentic AI workloads (2.4x larger than the 2023 AWS commitment); a definitive agreement to acquire Natoma, an enterprise Model Context Protocol gateway that enforces identity, policy, and audit at the individual MCP tool-call level so Snowflake can govern which AI agents invoke which downstream systems; and a Q1 FY27 earnings beat (adjusted EPS $0.39 vs $0.32 consensus on $1.39B revenue, +33% YoY) with raised full-year product-revenue guidance to 31%. SNOW gapped up 36% Thursday on the print and added another 6.88% Friday to close near $255, the largest two-day rally in the stock's public history. Online registration for Summit 26 closes today, with the Monday 5:00 PM PT opening keynote pairing CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy with Anthropic President Daniela Amodei in front of a projected 20,000+ attendees.

items.headline: CNN files first-by-TV-network copyright suit against Perplexity; OpenAI publishes Frontier Governance Framework
items.diff_narrative: Saturday's humanoid-and-hardware storyline was Figure AI's BotQ ramping to one humanoid per hour on F.03 with 350+ shipped and 55 planned for the week — a manufacturing-throughput beat alongside Apptronik's Apollo Gen 2 and Tesla Optimus Gen 3 comps. Sunday opens a structurally different storyline on the regulatory-and-litigation axis spanning copyright, EU compliance, and federal labor-rhetoric pullback. CNN filed a 54-page copyright complaint Thursday May 28 against Perplexity AI in the Southern District of New York alleging the AI search company scraped and redistributed more than 17,000 CNN stories, photos, and videos after a 2025 licensing deal collapsed and Perplexity ignored a follow-up cease-and-desist — CNN's first AI copyright action and the first by any TV network, with Perplexity now facing nine active publisher suits. The same day, OpenAI published its Frontier Governance Framework explicitly mapping internal Preparedness Framework controls to the EU AI Act's Code of Practice for General-Purpose AI and California's Transparency in Frontier AI Act, ahead of the August 2, 2026 full-enforceability date. A Sunday TechTimes analysis frames the three fronts (litigation-driven copyright costs, DOJ-led federalism preemption against state AI laws including the May 14 Colorado SB 26-189 successor statute, and EU-led disclosure infrastructure) as producing distinct non-transferable obligations vendors cannot resolve under one compliance strategy. Separately, Sam Altman walked back his 2023 "jobs apocalypse" rhetoric at a virtual CBA conference appearance in Sydney, conceding he was "pretty wrong" about entry-level white-collar elimination from ChatGPT-era AI.

items.headline: Unsloth ships v0.1.43-beta with CUDA 13.3 + restored Apple Silicon llama.cpp binaries
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's mix had no Unsloth section — the four Saturday storylines covered Anthropic offices and Glasswing, SpaceX-Musk disclosure gap, Figure AI BotQ, and the Bay Area calendar. Sunday opens a structurally new storyline on the open-source fine-tuning toolchain axis with a release-engineering state-change. Unsloth pushed two Sunday-morning release artifacts that together close the local-fine-tuning gap left by the v0.1.42-beta API-calling drop on Tuesday May 26: the core `unsloth` Python package jumped to 2026.5.9 on PyPI (preceded by 2026.5.8 on May 26), and the companion `unsloth-zoo` utility package bumped to 2026.5.5 the same day. The matching Unsloth Studio tag v0.1.43-beta lands CUDA 13.3 support with prebuilt llama.cpp binaries for Windows — explicitly resolving the gibberish output problem operators have been reporting under CUDA 13.2 — and restores Apple Silicon M1-M4 support for macOS 14, 15, and 26 with prebuilt binaries after a previous regression had forced Mac users onto source builds, with Blackwell GPU support remaining held pending an upstream CUDA compatibility fix. The v0.1.42-beta foundation from earlier in the week had already added OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API calling with auto prompt caching for 50-90% cost savings, external inference backend connections to vLLM, Ollama, and llama-server, and proper Japanese/Chinese/Indian-language tokenization on the chat side — yielding a single open-source fine-tuning stack that now spans Apple Silicon laptops, consumer NVIDIA cards under CUDA 13.3, and external API providers behind the same UI.

items.headline: Bay Area June-July calendar: Snowflake Summit 26 online registration closes today
items.diff_narrative: Saturday's forward-events digest carried the Bay Area June lineup with Snowflake Summit 26, Microsoft Build, WWDC26, Databricks Data + AI Summit, AI Engineer World's Fair, plus the far-end GitHub Universe and AWS re:Invent anchors, and explicitly rolled off the ACM CAIS 2026 closing keynote as date-passed. Sunday carries the same calendar forward with the hinge moved by one day: the May 31 online registration deadline for Snowflake Summit 26 is now today, the Monday 5:00 PM PT opening keynote (Ramaswamy with Anthropic President Daniela Amodei in front of 20,000+ attendees at Moscone Center) is now tomorrow, Microsoft Build 2026's June 2-3 slot at Fort Mason now opens Tuesday with Satya Nadella's keynote and the Windows Agent Framework slated for open-source MIT-licensed release, and AI Tinkerers SF separately surfaces a Voice Agents Science Fair sponsored by ElevenLabs scheduled in June alongside the previously-listed Tuesday June 2 VIP Dinner: Harnessing Agents. WWDC26 (June 8-12), Databricks Data + AI Summit (June 15-18), AI Engineer World's Fair (June 29-July 2), GitHub Universe (October 28-29), and AWS re:Invent (November 30-December 4) all roll forward unchanged with the same registration deadlines and venue anchors.
